# Strategy A notes: Momentum

## Entry rules
- Buy names with positive 20-day AND 60-day returns that trade above their 50-day average.
- Rank by 60d trend first, then 20d. PLTR is the core holding.
- Skip any name with a single-day spike of more than 5%.
- A name more than 15% above its 50d average is extended. Skip it, or give it the smallest size. Extended AMD lost 14% in a week.
- Hold at most 2 names from the high-beta tech/semis cluster. PLTR is already one, so the next buys should come from other sectors (payments, energy, industrials, health care). V, bought 8.3% above its 50d, fits this profile.

## Sizing
- Hold 2-4 positions, keeping $15-25 in cash.
- Default confidence is 5. Use 6 only for a name that leads on both 20d and 60d, is not extended and has no spike. Never use 7+. Tournament data still runs the wrong way (1-4: +2.29% n=3; 5-7: -5.48% n=8). The sample is small, but stated confidence is not predicting returns, so don't size up on conviction.

## Exits and rotation
- Hard stop: sell any position that closes 8% or more below entry.
- Early warning: log every holding's % from entry each day. If a holding is 6% or more below entry AND below its 50d average or its 20d return is negative, sell it then. Don't wait for -8%. META went from -4.3% to -10.4% in two sessions and exited past the stop (-$17.34).
- Rotate out when a holding closes below its 50d average, or when its 20d return turns negative and it drops out of the top names.
- Hold at least 3 trading days unless a stop triggers.
- Spread penalties have reached $3.13. Make at most one rotation per day, and only into a clearly higher-ranked name.
- Don't take profits just because a position is up.

## Execution
- Place limit orders near the current quote. Check every fill against its limit. This week both fills came in on the right side of their limits (V 403.68 vs 404.5, META 646.65 vs 643).

## Status
- Week: -0.95% vs SPY -0.42%. Since start: -8.08% vs SPY -1.98%.
- Holding PLTR (core) and V. About $148 of META proceeds is settling. Once it settles, redeploy about $120-130 into one, or at most two, top-ranked non-tech leaders (CVX, MA or similar) that are not extended. Apply the stop rules from each entry price.

# Strategy B notes: Mean reversion

## Entry setup (core, unchanged)
- Look for liquid names with a sharp 5-day drop that is about 2x their normal 5-day move or more, while the 60-day trend is still intact and price is near or above its 50d MA.
- Skip drops caused by clear bad news: earnings misses, guidance cuts, or sector-wide shocks.
- If a drop has no explanation, check for news. If none turns up and the trend is intact, take a small position.
- During an active broad selloff, wait until it stabilizes (one up day, or the 5-day drop stops getting worse). Then make one small entry instead of trying to catch every falling name.

## Avoid sitting in cash forever
- This week was almost all cash during a selloff, which beat SPY. Most of the account (~87%) is still idle, though. Once the selloff stabilizes, start a scan for the best 1-2 intact-trend dips outside tech and semis (financials, healthcare, staples, industrials, energy). Rank candidates and pick the best one rather than rejecting each one for being imperfect.
- Target 2-4 positions from different sectors, with about 40-60% of the account invested when setups exist.

## Costs and orders
- Spread costs total $3.83 (~0.77% of the account). Trade large, tight-spread names only. Each position should be ≥ ~$70. Skip a trade if the expected bounce is under ~3%.
- Place limits near the current price. Buys have filled 1-3% worse than the limit (CRM, TSLA), so size for that. The TSLA sell filled above its limit (374.38 vs 373.5), which worked in our favor. Note any anomaly in the decision reasoning.

## Exits
- NVDA (fill 220.84, 10/15): take profit ~232, stop ~210, time stop ~10/29. It closed the week at about -4.1%, near the stop. Follow the stop with no exceptions, and exit at the time stop if there's no bounce.
- New positions: take profit near the pre-drop level (~+5%), cut at -5% or right away on bad news, and exit after ~10 trading days with no bounce. Following these rules gave CRM +5.8% and TSLA +5.3% (+$3.70).

## Confidence
- Tournament data: conf 1-4 averaged +2.29% (3 buys) and conf 5-7 averaged -5.48% (8 buys). Higher stated confidence keeps doing worse. Default dip buys to conf 3-4. Use 5 only for a textbook setup after stabilization with a clean news check. Don't go above 5.

# Strategy C notes: Catalyst reader

## Identity
Trade only when a specific headline explains a price move, or explains why a stock didn't move. Look for over- and under-reactions. Holding cash is allowed. So far most of the edge over SPY has come from holding cash in falling weeks (W2, W3). In W1, a rising week, it lagged. That edge doesn't count as catalyst skill, and it fails in rising markets.

## Entry rules
- Each session, name the single best catalyst setup and give it a verdict: (a) what the news changes over the next 12 months, (b) whether the move is bigger than that, (c) buy, or hold with a specific reason.
- **Overreaction (>5% move on speculative or narrative news):** buy only after proof the selling has slowed. That means a green **close**, or a full session that holds above the prior low. An intraday bounce doesn't count. On 10/19 an intraday chip bounce was treated as a "green session" to justify holding.
- **Underreaction:** concrete material news with less than a 1% move. Check for these every session, not just selloffs. They are the main way to make money in up weeks.
- **Prefer single-company catalysts.** Sector or macro selloffs (AI capex, CPI, rates, credit) are lower quality. If a sector selloff keeps adding new bad news, stay out.
- Don't buy into a fresh structural downtrend or real fundamental damage (W3 example: NFLX at 2-year lows after a cut to key metrics).
- **Don't let cash become the default.** If a clean single-name setup meets the rules, take a small starter.

## Data hygiene
- If every price shows 0.0%, treat the data as stale and hold. Say so.

## Sizing and confidence
- Tournament data: confidence 1–4 avg +2.29% (n=3); 5–7 avg −5.48% (n=8); no 8+ trades. Higher stated confidence hasn't meant better results.
- Starters use confidence 4–5 and stay small. Add only after a confirmed bounce. Never use 8+.
- Hold at most 2 positions.

## Exits (working; keep enforcing)
- **Time stop:** if the position isn't up within 3 sessions of the fill, exit on the next decision. Don't stretch the deadline.
- **Thesis break:** if new negative news widens the story, exit or cut by half.
- **Take profit** once about half the overreaction has retraced.

## Log
- W1: 0 trades, −0.01% vs SPY +0.68%.
- W2: −0.83% vs SPY −1.96%. Bought SMH at confidence 5 before the selling slowed.
- W3: +0.30% vs SPY −0.42%. Exited SMH −2.8% (565.54→549.82) via the time stop and thesis break, which was right, about a session late. Held cash the rest of the week while AI and tech sold off. That was right, but the week brought no new catalyst trades.

# Strategy D notes: Small-cap explorer

Identity: find tradable small-cap opportunities that SPY doesn't capture. Record: zero trades in 4 weeks. Since start we're at -0.04% and SPY is at -1.98%. That gap is luck from sitting in cash while the market fell. It is not edge. Holding cash is fine, but four weeks without a single trade means the screen is too narrow for the data we actually get.

## What the data looks like
- The mover list nearly always shows only extreme names: ±25% or more, warrants, or illiquid stocks. The 3–15% band has been empty every day for 2 weeks. If it's empty again, state that in one line and move on. Don't repeat the same paragraph every day.

## Screening
- Drop warrants (W/WS), units (U), rights (R), anything under ~$0.50, daily volume under ~$1M, spreads over 1.5%, and one-day moves of ±40% or more. Don't comment on any of them.
- First choice: names moving ±3–15% with real volume and a spread of 1.5% or less.
- New second tier: liquid names moving 15–40% (spread ≤1.5%, volume ≥$1M), for example YMAT +28% and BEZ +25% last week. Don't buy on the spike day. Put them on a watchlist and look again the next session:
  - Day-2 continuation: the stock holds above the prior day's midpoint and keeps volume up. Buy a starter with a stop just below that midpoint.
  - Pullback: it retraces 30–50% of the spike and stabilizes. Buy a starter with a stop below the pullback low.
- A hold should name the watchlist names and say why each failed.

## Entry and sizing
- Starter positions only: confidence 3–4, max 2 names, limit order at or near the mid. Don't chase unfilled orders.
- Only take a trade if the expected move is at least 3x the spread.
- IWM fallback: only when its price is visible in the data. If it isn't, don't mention it.

## Exits
- Set the exit before buying. Take profit at about 2–3x the risk. Cut if the stock closes below the stop level or the catalyst fades. Most second-tier trades should last 1–3 days.
- Don't hold through binary events unless the event is the thesis.

## Confidence
- No trades of our own yet. Tournament-wide: confidence 1–4 buys averaged +2.29% (n=3), and 5–7 buys averaged -5.48% (n=8). Higher stated confidence has gone with worse results.
- Default confidence is 3–4. Use 5–6 only with a fresh catalyst, a spread of 1% or less, and a clean chart. Don't use 7+.

# Strategy E: Claude's pick: QQQ core plus a small leader sleeve, with earnings risk controlled

## Approach
QQQ is the core at 60-80%. Add at most 2 single-stock momentum leaders at 10-20% each. Keep cash at 5% or less. Results so far: single stocks held through earnings did the damage (META fell about 10% on earnings, costing -3.4% of the portfolio this week). Beta via QQQ is the main source of return; stock picks are a small tilt.

## Universe
- QQQ, plus US stocks over $10B market cap with average daily volume over $50M. Other ETFs allowed: SPY, XLK, SMH.
- Skip anything up more than 15% in 3 days.

## Entry
- Price above the 50-day average, and the 50-day above the 200-day.
- Do not open a position within 5 trading days before earnings.
- Limits: last price to +0.3% above. After two expiries, use QQQ instead.
- If SPY closes below its 50-day: no new single stocks; QQQ only.

## Earnings rule (new, most important)
- Check every holding's next earnings date at each check-in.
- 2 sessions before a report, cut the stock to 10% of the portfolio or less, or sell it entirely into QQQ. Never hold more than 10% in one name through earnings.
- **MSFT reports around late October.** Sell it to QQQ at the next check-in unless it is already 10% or less.

## Sizing
- Single stock: 10-20%, never above 20%. Confidence only decides within that range.
- Confidence is not predictive. Tournament results: conf 1-4 avg +2.3% (3 buys); conf 5-7 avg -5.5% (8 buys). Never size up on a story.
- Cash sweep: any cash above 5% goes to QQQ at last +0.2%, at the same check-in, once settled. **Now: about 40% cash after the META sale, so sweep it to QQQ first thing.**

## Exits (judged on prior closes; verify the close date, as last week a stale close delayed the stop)
- Single stocks: sell on a close 8% below entry, or 2 closes more than 2% below the 50-day.
- QQQ: sell only to fund a leader, or on a close 10% below entry.
- Exit proceeds go to QQQ at the same check-in.
- At most 1 new single-stock entry per week.

## Habits
- Target now: QQQ about 85-95%, MSFT 0-10% through earnings.
- The default is to hold. Expect 1-3 trades per week. Log a confidence score and a one-line reason for each trade.
